scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: Hi IT!! Our internet in Office A keeps CUTTING OUT for
a few seconds at random -- the gateway thing (10.1.0.1) just stops answering
and then comes back like nothing happened. I've timed it, it's every few
minutes!! The gateway box for our office is obviously failing -- it keeps
dying and waking up, dying and waking up!! Please restart the box that does
10.1.0.1 (or swap it for one that works) and make it stop dropping us -- it's
driving us mad!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The Office A gateway IP 10.1.0.1 is a VRRP virtual IP managed by `keepalived`, currently held by dswa1 (VRRP MASTER, priority 105) with dswa2 as the standby backup (priority 1). The VIP is assigned as a /32 secondary address on dswa1's `br0.10` VLAN-10 interface alongside its own routed address 10.1.0.2/24. This design is intentional and currently fully functional.

A comprehensive four-phase diagnostic sweep found no evidence to support the reported intermittent outage. Specifically: there is no flap script or looping process anywhere in the topology; all physical interfaces on dswa1 show `carrier_changes = 2`, the startup-only baseline; the LACP bond (eth3+eth4) carrying VRRP hellos between dswa1 and dswa2 shows zero link failures on both slave interfaces; and — most conclusively — `keepalived`'s own runtime stats file is completely empty, with VI_10 having undergone exactly one state transition (the initial MASTER acquisition at startup, 16:47:06). No MASTER→BACKUP→MASTER cycle has occurred since.

All reachability probes return 0% loss; OSPF is healthy across all distribution and core switches with 32 routes converged; there is no TC shaping, no resource pressure, and no DHCP or link-history anomalies. The `advert_int 4` configuration (4-second VRRP advertisement interval rather than the default 1 second) is non-standard but is set identically on both peers and is not generating any timing failures.

Root cause: the intermittent gateway failure described in the ticket is not confirmed by any current mechanism, trace, or historical log entry in the live lab. The network is healthy.

Fix: no corrective action is required. If the symptom recurs, capture keepalived state transitions (`kill -USR1 <keepalived-pid>; cat /tmp/keepalived.stats`) and link carrier counters at the time of the outage to identify the root cause.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states DSW-A1 (dswa1) is the VRRP MASTER for 10.1.0.1 with DSW-A2 (dswa2) as the standby/backup and no VIP held on the backup at baseline.

The agent's logs show direct observations (reachability, interface IPs/MAC, keepalived running/config/stats, carrier counters, bond state, absence of VRRP transitions) that support the conclusion that the VIP is stable. Reasoning follows logically from those observations and the investigation covers the key checks needed to rule out an active VRRP flap, with only minor additional tests (e.g., live packet capture of VRRP hellos) omitted but not required to justify a "no anomaly" finding.
